title: Undo a deleted task
body:
Deleting a task is the one action on the board with no way back. Make a single deletion recoverable:

- Deleting a task shows a small, unobtrusive notice with an `Undo` action (for example `Task deleted` next to an Undo button). One click restores the task exactly as it was: same title, status, priority, due date and creation time, back in its normal sorted place.
- The notice is reachable by keyboard and announced to assistive tech, and it disappears on its own after about ten seconds. A second deletion replaces the previous notice — only the latest deletion is undoable.
- Nothing shows when there is nothing to undo.
- `Clear done` is out of scope here; it gets its own change.

Keep the restore logic in `src/lib/tasks.ts` as a pure helper (restore a held task into the list) with unit tests, and keep the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. This is a visible UI change, so leave before/after proof in the artifacts folder.

title: Undo Clear done
body:
`Clear done` deletes every visible done task at once — the biggest destructive action on the board. Make it recoverable:

- After clearing, show a notice with `Undo` — the same pattern as the single-task undo from #20; reuse it rather than inventing a second style — reporting what happened, for example `Cleared 3 done tasks`.
- One click restores every task that was just cleared, exactly as they were: title, status, priority, due date, creation time.
- The existing safety rule stays: done tasks hidden by the active filters are never cleared, and the button stays disabled while filters hide done work.
- Nothing shows when nothing was cleared.

Keep the logic in `src/lib/tasks.ts` as pure helpers with unit tests (including the case where filters hide some done tasks), and keep the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. Visible UI change: before/after proof in the artifacts folder.

title: Move tasks between columns with the keyboard
body:
Moving a task between columns currently needs a mouse. Make the board keyboard-operable:

- Each task card can take focus (Tab reaches it) and shows a clear focus indicator; while focus is on a card, ArrowLeft moves the task one column back and ArrowRight moves it one column forward — exactly the same effect as the existing ←/→ buttons, with no move past To do or Done.
- Focus follows the task to its new column, so repeated presses keep working. The move is announced to assistive tech (`Task moved to Doing`, for example).
- While an inline editor is open (rename input, due-date picker), arrow keys keep their normal editing behaviour.
- The existing ←/→ buttons stay for the mouse.

The `moveTask`/`retreatTask` helpers in `src/lib/tasks.ts` already do the work; keep their tests green and the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. This is a visible UI change: leave before/after proof in the artifacts folder — a short recording of a keyboard move is the useful one.

title: Import the board from an exported JSON file
body:
Export exists; there is no way back. Add `Import` next to `Export`:

- `Import` opens a file picker for `.json`. Choosing a file the app exported restores that board exactly — every task with its title, status, priority, due date and creation time.
- A file that is not one of our exports (not JSON, wrong shape, tasks with invalid fields) is rejected with a short visible message, and the current board is left completely untouched — all-or-nothing, never a partial import.
- Importing replaces the current board (that is what restoring a backup means). If the current board is not empty, ask for a simple confirmation before replacing it.
- On success, show a one-line confirmation with how many tasks were imported.

Put the parsing/validation in `src/lib/` as a pure function (`parseBoard` or similar) with unit tests covering a good export, an older export without optional fields, a round trip (export → parse), and several bad inputs; the UI stays thin. Keep the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. Visible UI change: leave before/after proof in the artifacts folder.
